derivation.note: BLS publishes the payroll LEVEL. The headline number the market reacts to is the month-over-month change, computed here.

move.detail: -104k. Bigger in magnitude than 56% of the 55 moves since 2022-03-01. The typical move is 119.3k; this is 0.7 sigma.

impact.meaning: A RISE in this series pushes mortgage rates UP. A fall pushes them DOWN.

chains.chain: Payrolls → ↓ Recession risk → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Recession fear is the classic bid for duration. Yields fall.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

chains.chain: Payrolls → ↑ Growth expectations → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Payrolls are the highest-frequency growth read.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

chains.chain: Payrolls → ↑ Fed policy stance → ↑ 2Y Treasury → ↑ 10Y Treasury → ↑ MBS yield → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Strong hiring removes the case for easing.
The front end prices the expected path of policy.
Front-end repricing pulls the belly and the long end, but only partly.
MBS are priced off the Treasury curve. This is the main channel.
Lenders price off MBS execution, with a short lag for rate sheets.

chains.chain: Payrolls → ↑ Fed policy stance → ↑ QT / MBS runoff → ↑ MBS spread → ↑ 30Y mortgage rate
rationales: Strong hiring removes the case for easing.
A hawkish Fed keeps runoff going.
Fed MBS runoff removes the largest price-insensitive buyer from the market.
A wider spread raises the borrower rate even when Treasuries are unchanged.
